title: Ideay, y vos qué
desc: Five years before anybody asks you what you actually think
setting: You are on the corner with Marcos, he has been talking about a cousin who wants to leave, and he has turned to face you.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y vos qué? ¿Vos qué pensás de este país?
steps.en: Ideay, and you? What do you think of this country?

options.en: Do you really want me to tell you?
options.feedback: Check first, because for five years that question has meant do you like the lake. This time it does not, and he will say so.

options.en: I like it a lot, honestly.
options.feedback: That is the tourist answer and he has heard you give it two hundred times. He asked a different question tonight.

options.en: That is a big question, maje.
options.feedback: It is, and he knows. Buying a second does no harm as long as you then answer it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Sí, hombre. De verdad. Ya llevás cinco años aquí.
steps.en: Yes, man. Really. You have been here five years now.

options.es: Que es el país más difícil que conozco y no me quiero ir.
options.en: That it is the hardest country I know and I do not want to leave.
options.feedback: Both halves in one sentence. Anything that is only praise or only complaint tells him you are still outside it.

options.es: Que la gente es lo mejor que tiene.
options.en: That the people are the best thing about it.
options.feedback: True and it is what every visitor says. He is standing there waiting for the other half.

options.en: That it still has a long way to go.
options.feedback: A verdict on somebody else's country delivered from the corner. Even when it is true, that sentence needs to be his, not yours.

options.es: Por lo que le pasa a tu primo. Por eso se va.
options.en: Because of what is happening to your cousin. That is why he is going.
options.feedback: You answered with the thing he was already talking about instead of a general opinion. That is arguing about a country from inside it.

options.en: Because of the money, above all.
options.feedback: Right and broad. Naming his cousin would have made it a conversation instead of an assessment.

options.es: Por muchas cosas que mejor no digo.
options.en: For a lot of reasons I had better not say.
options.feedback: He asked you straight after five years of not asking. Hiding behind mejor no digo wastes the one time it was a real question.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay. Y aun así te quedás.
steps.en: Ideay. And even so you stay.

options.es: Aquí está mi mujer, mi hijo y vos. ¿Para dónde me voy a ir?
options.en: My wife is here, my son is here and so are you. Where would I go?
options.feedback: The answer is a list of people, which is the only answer that means anything on that corner.
Enough. He gave you the whole opening and you used four words of it.

options.en: For now, we will see later.
options.feedback: Said to a man whose cousin is leaving next month, por ahora sounds like one foot already out of the door.
